sections.h2: Where does Newton County fit in the Atlanta region?
sections.html:
East of Atlanta, Newton County counts Covington as both seat and biggest city. Georgia's General Assembly set it up on December 24, 1821, and the name honors a sergeant who fought under Gen. Francis Marion in the Revolutionary War, per Wikipedia. Terrain is Piedmont, and most of the county drains toward the Upper Ocmulgee River; a sliver in the east runs to the Upper Oconee.

Covington shares the map with four more cities: Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle. Newborn is a town, and Starrsville is unincorporated. Interstate 20 and US 278 cut through, joined by state routes 11, 20, 36, 81, 138, 142, 162 and 212. The adjoining counties are Walton, Morgan, Jasper, Butts, Henry and Rockdale.

Hollywood found the courthouse square. Crews shot the first five Dukes of Hazzard episodes around Covington in late 1978, and In the Heat of the Night filmed there from 1988 to 1995. Schools come mostly from the Newton County School System, with some Social Circle addresses served by that city's own district. The county also claims to be where Georgia 4-H began: canning and corn clubs started in 1904 took the 4-H name in 1906.

sections.h2: How quickly has Newton County grown, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Newton County had 41,808 residents in 1990 and 112,483 at the 2020 count; the July 2025 estimate stands at 125,583. The 2000 count was 62,001 and the 2010 count 99,958, so the sharpest jump came in the 2000s.

Workers spend 35.9 minutes getting to their jobs on average, and households average 2.83 people. Land area is 273.80 square miles. In 2020, 70.2% of occupied homes were owner-occupied, 5.5% of the 41,756 units were vacant and the median resident was 38.0 years old.

sections.h2: Where do I pay or ask questions about Newton County property tax?
sections.html:
Pay in person at the Tax Commissioner's Admin Building at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101 in Covington, or to the Westside office at 3612 Salem Rd. Each opens at 8:00 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, and 770-784-2020 reaches both, according to the office's locations page.

  • Tax Assessors, 770-784-2030: returns, exemptions, appeals and value questions
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and balances; an elected office, separate from the assessors and the county commission
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set the millage rates
  • Deed room at the Newton County Courthouse: copies of recorded deeds

Self-service kiosks stand inside Kroger on Highway 20 South and on Highway 278 NE. The commissioner's home page also publishes a delinquent tax list, refreshed every quarter, and a page on excess funds. A written balance request can be mailed to the Admin Building.

sections.h2: What is the Newton County tax due date, and what happens if it is missed?
sections.html:
Newton County bills come due each November 15, an earlier date than the old December 20 that applied before the 2026 tax year. Commissioners adopted the change in 2025, as the office's FAQ explains.

That 2026 deadline landed on a Sunday, so the office gave until Monday, November 16 with no interest. Real estate and personal property statements are mailed by September 15, while non-homesteaded mobile homes get a statement by February 1 and pay by April 1.

  • Late interest is figured monthly at prime plus 3% a year, and the page listed .0875% per month
  • After 120 days a penalty of 5% of the original tax is added, and it repeats every 120 days up to a combined 20%
  • Mail counts only with a U.S. Postal Service postmark; meter postmarks are rejected
  • The office takes partial payments, but charges keep building on the unpaid remainder

Cards add 2.35% (Visa, MasterCard, Discover) or 3% (American Express), each with a $1.50 floor. An online eCheck costs a flat $1.50. Subdivisions that opted in to pay for street lights see a separate street light fee on the statement, and the revenue the bill raises goes to county government, schools, roads and bridges, courts and the jail, fire protection, public health, parks and libraries.

sections.h2: How does the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant show up on a Newton County bill?
sections.html:
The credit prints on its own line marked HTRG Credit and comes off the current taxes due before the total. For 2026, eligible homesteaded properties get an $18,000 cut in assessed value for purposes of the credit, and the dollar result varies by tax district.

Owners file nothing extra with the Tax Commissioner. The credit rides on an existing homestead exemption, and it sits alongside that exemption rather than replacing it. The office describes it as good for the 2026 tax year alone.

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, call the lender: the tax office has no say over escrow amounts, and a smaller bill may leave the mortgage payment unchanged.

sections.h2: Which Newton County homestead exemptions exist, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
Apply by April 1, or inside the 45-day window that follows assessment notices. One filing lasts until ownership or your primary residence changes, and exemptions never transfer to a buyer.

  • Standard: $4,000 off taxable value on county and school levies, one homestead per owner
  • Age 62: $20,000 off county and school levies, with a $15,000 cap on net earned income
  • Age 65: $30,000 off county levies and $50,000 off Newton Schools, with a $25,000 earned income cap
  • Disabled veteran: up to $126,526 off the 40% taxable value, backed by a Veterans Administration letter

The two senior exemptions also limit household social security and retirement income to $99,648, per the homestead page. To contest a value, write to the Board of Assessors inside 45 days of the notice and say which appeal route you pick; Board of Equalization is one option.

sections.h2: What should a Newton County seller know about liens before closing?
sections.html:
A FiFa is the lien Newton County records for unpaid tax, entered on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. A 30-day notice of intent goes to the owner of record before one is filed.

Once recorded, a FiFa lasts seven years and can be renewed again and again. Because the filing is public, credit bureaus can see it; settling the tax, fees, penalties and interest clears it. The office does not sell liens over the counter and posts a list when a tax sale is set.

Ask for a written balance dated near closing, then have the closing agent settle it out of proceeds. Because statements go to the owner, not to the lender, pass your bill along if a servicer needs it.

faqs.q: When is Newton County property tax due each year?
faqs.a: On November 15, a date that replaced December 20 beginning with the 2026 tax year. In 2026 the no-interest window ran through Monday, November 16 because November 15 was a Sunday.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Newton County valuation?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the assessment notice date. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors, pick your method, and rest it on value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption.

faqs.q: Will my Newton County homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Exemptions do not move with the house, a point the office makes plainly. The buyer files a new application, due April 1 or during the 45-day appeal window.

faqs.q: What are the Newton County tax office hours and addresses?
faqs.a: The Admin Building is at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101, and the Westside office is at 3612 Salem Rd, both in Covington. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, and the phone is 770-784-2020.

faqs.q: Which cities and towns sit inside Newton County?
faqs.a: Covington is the seat, joined by Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle, plus the town of Newborn. A city address may also carry a city levy, so read the whole bill.
